_comment: Piper TTS cast. `model` is a piper voice name (auto-downloaded into the voices dir); `speaker` is the index into that model's speaker_id_map. length_scale is DURATION: higher = slower. vctk defaults to 1.4, libritts_r to 1.0, so scales are not comparable across models. noise_scale controls pitch/timbre variability (low = flat, controlled); noise_w controls phoneme-duration variability (low = clipped, high = loose). Speakers were chosen by measuring median F0 of every candidate rather than by guesswork — the vctk_id and hz fields record what was measured, so a swap can be made on evidence. Accents noted where the VCTK corpus documents them.

narrator.note: Carries most of the prose. Mid male, unhurried, deliberately NOT Oliver so the two never blur.

oliver.note: Oliver's interior voice. p226 is documented in the VCTK corpus as male, 22, from Surrey — Home Counties, so RP-adjacent posh. 109Hz is semi-deep. length_scale pushed well above the 1.4 default for the sleepiness, noise_w pulled down so it drawls rather than wanders.

furthermore.note: The deepest voice in the whole 109-speaker corpus at 78Hz. Very slow, and both noise values floored: flat affect, no emphasis, nothing hurried. Calmly disinterested — an elephant who regards language as a fad.

revilo.note: Deliberately the SAME speaker as Oliver. The text says he has Oliver's face with everything moved a sixteenth of an inch, and speaks in Oliver's cadence with Oliver's pause before the last word — so: identical voice, faster and looser. Same man, better rested, worse intentions.

_attributes._comment: Skill voices are Oliver's interior arguing with itself, so they stay in his head — same model, four facets by attribute.

asimov.note: Deep and deliberate. Explains the impossible slowly enough that it almost survives.

albert.note: Second-deepest available. Enormous patience, impeccable courtesy, forty years of practice at not being a nuisance.

sir_jerry.note: Older, formal, measured — a knight surveying a field.

soliloquy.note: Female, theatrical, room-filling. Loose noise_w so the verse has swing in it.

ginny.note: Fast and clipped. Nothing wasted; every sentence a stance.

chef_d.note: Ancient and slow. Her scripted lisp ('Shit down, shit down') is already phonetic, so it is left untouched and comes out correctly.

bud.note: Fast, tense, over-committed. A man holding up a building with his mouth.

woolbinkle.note: Recast. p285 measured only 14Hz of pitch variance on a controlled line — flatter than the median — against a brief of hurried, self-interrupting eagerness, and raising noise_scale barely moved it because inherent prosody dominates. p232 measures 23.5Hz at a near-identical register. p316 measured 142Hz and was rejected: 31% of its frames jump above 1.7x the median, which is octave error in the pitch tracker rather than expression. noise_scale pushed to 0.80: a sweep showed the lever moves variance only from ~21 to ~24 across its whole range, with run-to-run noise of about 3, so this is close to the ceiling. He now sits just above the cast median rather than below it. The corpus holds exactly one strongly expressive male in this register — p374 — and it went to T, whose brief needs it more.

landy.note: Brisk and tidy. Everything is filed, stamped and completely sorted.

t.note: Recast. p258 measured a pitch variance of 10Hz — the second flattest voice in the cast — for a character whose brief is theatrical alliterative soliloquy, and noise_w was already at 0.50 so tuning could not reach it. p374 sits at the same pitch (113 vs 114Hz) so his register is unchanged, and measures 45Hz variance: the most expressive male in the whole 109-speaker corpus.

dee.note: One half of Dee Stroii. See dee_two: a near-identical pitch from a different speaker, so the two of him are uncannily close without being the same.

dee_two.note: The other one. Same measured pitch as dee, different speaker.

darek.note: American, warm, unhurried — the drawl is written into the text ('wetter'n a boiled owl'), so the voice only has to be slow and kind. length_scale raised from 1.24 after measurement put him at 4.3 words/sec, well above the median, which is the one thing Darek must never be. Raised a second time: on a controlled line he was still quicker than the median, and Darek is the man who has all evening.

ben.note: Recast. Brief is eighty-eight, deep, slow and entirely unbothered; 7704 measured the fastest pace in the cast at 5.3 words/sec with 36Hz variance. 3368 is deeper (91 vs 102Hz) and far flatter (13.5Hz), and length_scale is well up for the slowness. length_scale raised again after a controlled measurement still put him above median pace; at eighty-eight he should be the slowest American in the parish.

mary.note: Recast. Brief is long slow observations from a half-shut iguana who is never asleep; 5618 measured 68Hz of pitch variance — the most animated voice in the entire cast, three times the median. 1923 measures 15Hz and sits slightly lower, with length_scale raised so nothing about her is hurried.

fatty.note: Fast and delighted. Donut metaphysics delivered at speed.

wino_t.note: On the beat. Fastest in the cast — his bars are slash-separated in the text and the normaliser turns each slash into a line break so the rhythm lands.

barney.note: Warm and broad. Slips into a children's-television register about the weather and does not notice.

luigi.note: Animated and quick. The Italian-American cadence is in the written syntax ('Is not a job. Is a vocation.'), so the voice supplies the energy.

instagator.note: Recast. The brief is the flattest delivery in the cast, and both noise values were already floored at 0.20 — yet speaker 3307 still measured 43Hz of pitch variance, the fourth most expressive voice here. That is the speaker's own nature, not a setting. 6458 holds nearly the same pitch (129 vs 132Hz) and measures 13Hz. An alligator discussing assassination in the register of a quarterly review.
